name: MD-05
label: Safe D

key_factors: Open seat after Hoyer's retirement, but Democratic nominee Boafo heavily funded with large outside support
Republican Chaffee shows minimal fundraising and no visible campaign infrastructure
Prediction markets price Democratic win at ~97%
model.rationale: This Maryland district leans Democratic by 17 points, and the Democratic nominee has raised over $1.6 million with more than $12 million in outside support, while the Republican shows no reported fundraising. Markets price a Democratic win near certainty, consistent with the fundamentals.
model.watch: Any late surge in Republican outside spending or a polling surprise showing the race inside single digits would warrant a downgrade.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.
Open seat: Steny Hoyer (D) is not on the ballot.

overview:
Steny Hoyer's retirement opens this southern Maryland seat, but the district's D+17 partisan lean keeps it firmly in Democratic hands on paper. Democrat Adrian Boafo enters the general election with strong financial backing, including roughly $12 million in outside support and no outside money opposing him.

Republican Chris Chaffee reports little fundraising activity, and no public polls or expert ratings track the race. Prediction markets put the Democratic chance around 97%. The seat remains Safe Democratic, with the main uncertainty being the usual open-seat transition rather than a genuine competitive threat.
